profile.name: Amis harvest dance
profile.tagline: Interlinked arms in an ever-open circle.
profile.insight: At the Amis Harvest Festival, young men and women dance hand in hand around elders, choosing partners and selecting future tribe leaders through dance and ritual.
profile.profile: The Amis harvest dance is performed during the Ilisin Harvest Festival in Taiwan, where men and women of all ages form hand-in-hand circles around elders. The dance features walking, running, and jumping movements, with songs led by a soloist and chorus. It serves both as a communal celebration of the harvest and a social event for partner selection and leadership selection.
profile.profile_long: The Amis harvest dance is an integral part of the Ilisin Harvest Festival, celebrated by the Amis indigenous people of Taiwan, primarily in the Taitung and Hualien areas during lunar July and August. This festival marks the completion of the rice harvest, replacing the earlier millet harvest ceremonies. The dance is performed by men and women of all ages, who wear traditional festival costumes and form hand-in-hand circles around the elders seated at the center. The dance movements include walking, running, and jumping, with coastal tribes exhibiting more complex and variable steps than those in mountainous regions. Singing accompanies the dance, typically with a lead singer initiating a chorus that others follow, serving as a medium to communicate with ancestral spirits and gods. The dance also functions as a social mechanism for young Amis men and women to select partners, with girls actively joining boys they favor during the dance. Elders, who hold a respected status, observe the dance and select potential future tribe leaders through this ritual. The festival includes other important ceremonies such as the adult ceremony, which marks the transition of boys into adulthood through training and tests, including a running race. The priest, a knowledgeable figure responsible for agricultural rituals and communication with the gods, oversees the festival. The dance and festival are deeply connected to the agricultural calendar, ancestral worship, and social structure of the Amis community.

sections.origins_and_history: The Amis Harvest Festival, also called Ilisin, Malalikid, or Kiloma'an, is a traditional indigenous festival in Taiwan celebrated after the rice harvest, primarily in the Taitung and Hualien regions. It evolved from earlier millet harvest ceremonies and is held between July and September according to the lunar calendar. The festival lasts from one to seven days depending on the tribe and includes rituals to honor ancestral gods and pray for future prosperity. The harvest dance is a central communal activity during the festival.
sections.how_it_is_danced: Dancers form a hand-in-hand circle around elders seated in the center. Movements include walking, running, and jumping, with coastal tribes performing more complex steps. A lead singer initiates songs that the group follows. Young men and women dance together, with partner selection occurring through proximity and gestures such as placing betel nuts into a boy's bag. The dance is rhythmic and communal, emphasizing social bonds and respect for elders.
sections.music_and_instruments: Songs are led by a soloist with a chorus response, serving as communication with ancestors and gods. The lyrics vary by age group and tribe, with adult songs focusing on real-life themes like farming and fishing, and children's songs being more imaginative. Specific instruments are not described in the sources.
sections.costume_and_setting: Participants wear traditional festival clothes, including hats decorated with rooster feathers indicating status. The dance takes place around a campfire during the festival nights, often under the full moon, creating a communal and ceremonial atmosphere.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: The dance is performed during the Ilisin Harvest Festival to celebrate the harvest, honor ancestors, and ensure future prosperity. It also serves social functions such as partner selection among youth and the selection of future tribe leaders by elders. The festival includes rites of passage like the adult ceremony for boys transitioning to manhood.
sections.notable_figures: The priest plays a central role, overseeing agricultural rituals and communication with the gods. The priest must be knowledgeable about the calendar, weather, tribal history, dance, and spiritual communication. Elders also hold important roles in observing the dance and selecting future leaders.
sections.regional_variants: The dance movements vary between coastal and mountainous tribes, with coastal dances being more complex. The timing and duration of the festival also differ among tribes.
sections.lineage: The Amis harvest dance is a traditional indigenous dance of Taiwan, linked closely to agricultural cycles and ancestral worship. It shares communal circle dance elements with other indigenous and East Asian harvest dances but is distinct in its social functions and ritual context.

profile.sacred_note: The dance is part of sacred harvest ceremonies involving ancestral worship and rituals led by the priest; outsiders should respect the ritual context and not disrupt ceremonies.

claims.text: The “Harvest Festival”, also known as the “Harvest Ceremony”, is one of the most important festival for indigenous tribes in Taiwan and it is held to celebrate the harvest.
claims.quote: The “Harvest Festival”, also known as the “Harvest Ceremony”, is one of the most important festival for indigenous tribes in Taiwan and it  is held to celebrate the harvest.

claims.text: The ceremony lasts approximately seven days and is held during July, August, and September.
claims.quote: The ceremony lasts approximately seven days. The “Harvest Festival” is held during July, August, and September.

claims.text: The Amis Harvest Festival is held on the full moon day after the autumn harvest.
claims.quote: Amis Harvest Festival is held on the full moon day after the autumn harvest.

claims.text: Men and women, young and old, wearing festival costumes, led by a singer, dance hand in hand.
claims.quote: At that time, the men and women, the young and old wearing festival costumes, led by a singer, dance with hand in hand.

claims.text: The young Amis men and women take singing and dancing as important for choosing partners.
claims.quote: The young Amis men and women will take singing and dancing as an important thing for them to choose their partners.

claims.text: Girls actively stand by boys they like and dance with them.
claims.quote: When a girl finds a boy she likes, she will actively stand by the boy and dance with him.

claims.text: Elders sit in the middle and youths dance around them, proposing toasts and selecting future leaders.
claims.quote: In the party of the ceremony, the elder people sit in the middle and the youths will dance around the elders and propose a toast with the elders.

claims.text: The priest leads the sacrificial ritual and instructs farming activities; he must know the calendar, weather, history, dance, and how to communicate with gods.
claims.quote: The ceremony will be hosted by the priest of the tribe, who is in charge of the sacrificial ritual... it is necessary for a priest to know the calendar, the weather, the history of the tribe, the dancing and how to communicate with the gods.

claims.text: Songs are a medium to communicate with the soul of ancestors and gods; adult songs focus on real-life themes, children's songs are more imaginary.
claims.quote: The songs are regarded as the media through which the people communicate with the soul of the ancestors and the god... The lyrics of the children's song tend to be imaginary and the one of adults are more relevant to the things in reality.

claims.text: Dancing is mostly walking, running, and jumping; coastal dances are more complicated than mountainous ones.
claims.quote: The movements in the dance are mostly walking, running and jumping... the dance movements around coastal areas are more complicated and changeable than tribes in mountainous areas.

claims.text: The night of Valentine's Day is the last night of the festival, where young people dance around the campfire and confess love.
claims.quote: The night of Valentine's Day is the last night of the Harvest Festival... girls and boys dance around the campfire under the moonlight and confess to the one whom she or he loves.

claims.text: Girls put betel into the bag of the boy they like; if he reciprocates, they become a couple.
claims.quote: Later, a girl puts the betel into the bag of the boy she likes. If the boy also likes her, he will give his bag to the girl. They then become a couple later.
